fix: Delete probe.rs (marked TEMPORARY, not for commit), its `pub mod probe;` line in src/lib.rs, the call sites tree/reconciliation.rs (span(1) near line 991, span(4) near line 2306) and scrolling/layout.rs (span(0) near line 2968), and benches/scroll_probe.rs. If the timer must stay, use incular_core::time instead of std::time::Instant::now.

Replace the flat_map/vec![]/collect chain with a loop over a Vec::with_capacity(menu.entries.len()): Menu => children.push(build_menu_node(..)?), Item => children.push(build_item_node(..)?), Group => for (group_index, item) in group.items.iter().enumerate() { children.push(build_item_node(item, &format!(..), ids, callbacks)?) }, Divider => children.push(PlatformMenuSnapshotNode { .. }). This removes one single-element Vec per entry, the intermediate Vec per group and the Result collect.

Stop formatting a path String for every node (also at lines 1098, 1104, 1115, 1122), even when the node has an explicit id. Thread one reusable `path: &mut String` through build_menu_node/build_item_node: record `let len = path.len();`, `write!(path, ".menu.{index}")`, recurse, then `path.truncate(len)`. Only call MenuItemId::generated(path) when menu.id/item.id is None.

install() rebuilds the full snapshot (BTreeSet, Strings, Vec nodes, format! paths) on every call, including every widget rebuild via reconcile_from -> install_if_bound (tree/reconciliation.rs:516 and :436), and only then compares with the installed snapshot. Skip the rebuild when the declarative model is unchanged: have PlatformMenuBar::update/reconcile_from compare the incoming menus with the current ones (or set a generation flag when they differ) and call install only on change. Callback-only changes still need the callback rebuild, so keep a path that rebuilds only callbacks.

Move instead of cloning the menu Vec: `let menus = std::mem::take(&mut incoming.state.borrow_mut().menus);` (the incoming binding is a freshly built widget state that is discarded after reconciliation). Verify at tree/reconciliation.rs:516 that the incoming binding is not reused before relying on this.
Read the flag without cloning the whole menu tree: `.field("installed", &self.inner.state.borrow().installed.is_some())`.

The shared RefCell borrow of binding state is held while install() calls delegate methods (acquire, set_event_handler, set_menus). Hold the menus as an owned handle instead, e.g. store `menus: Rc<[PlatformMenu]>` and do `let menus = Rc::clone(&self.state.borrow().menus); self.controller.install(&menus)`. The same pattern appears in install_if_bound (line 1012).

BuildContext::locales() (tree/context.rs:231) returns a freshly collected Vec on every call, and this runs on every build of every ProviderImage. Add a `BuildContext::primary_locale(&self) -> Option<Locale>` that reads only the first entry, and write: `if let Some(locale) = context.primary_locale() {`.

stream() runs on every build and always builds the key (cloning the provider Rc and moving in a configuration whose Option<Locale> may own Strings) before comparing. Compare against the stored key by reference first, and build the owned key only on a miss: `if let (Some((provider, cfg)), Some(s)) = (resolved.as_ref(), stream.as_ref()) && provider == &config.provider && *cfg == configuration { return s.clone(); }` then construct `(config.provider.clone(), configuration)` after the early return.

Every build with a semantic label allocates a new String via label.clone(). Store the label as a shared immutable string (`semantic_label: Option<Arc<str>>` or Rc<str>) and have Semantics::label (widgets semantics.rs:77) accept that shared type, so the per-build step is a refcount bump. Keep Semantics::label(impl Into<String>) only if no other caller needs the change.

RadioGroup::value and RadioGroup::on_changed are stored but never read, and the From impl discards them, so callers who set them get no behavior. Either propagate the group value and callback to the RawRadio children (for example via the group's selection state), or delete the value/on_changed fields and their setters so RadioGroup is only a plain wrapper and the doc comment matches the code.
